For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the eggs came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-eggs" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-eggs-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of eggs, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach eggs

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach eggs comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Eggs, as sold from Hg mining area (Wuchuan) (mining-affected area) had Zn higher at 61,800 µg/kg, against 310 µg/kg for background area (Anshun) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/guo2024-duck-eggs-hg-mining-china|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guo Y, Li Y, Wang Q, Zhang H, Liu J, Feng X · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guo2024-duck-eggs-hg-mining-china">Heavy metal contamination in duck eggs near mercury mining areas in southwest China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/guo2024-duck-eggs-hg-mining-china">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, eggs, as sold from HEM diet + 0.4 mg Se/kg as selenized yeast (HEM+Se) (experiment) had Se higher at 1,640 µg/kg, against 610 µg/kg for hens fed corn-soybean meal basal diet (control, CON) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wu et al. · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens">Ameliorative effects of selenized yeast on laying hen performance and heavy metal residues in eggs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Veterinary Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that eggs, as sold from 100% of soybean oil replaced by black soldier fly larvae oil (experiment) had aluminium higher at 3,660 µg/kg, against 2,210 µg/kg for control diet, corn-soybean meal with soybean oil (CON) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/kim2022-bsf-larvae-oil-eggs-heavy-metals|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kim YB, Jeon JY, Kim NR, Chae HS, Kim JS, Kim HJ, Oh SI, Cho S, Lee KW · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kim2022-bsf-larvae-oil-eggs-heavy-metals">Dietary effects of black soldier fly larvae oil on laying hen performance, egg quality, and egg safety</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Animal Bioscience</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kim2022-bsf-larvae-oil-eggs-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

class="cite-card-authors">Song Y, Wang Y, Mao W, Sui H, Yong L, Yang D, Jiang D, Zhang L, Gong Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" ONE 12(5): e0177978</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/song2017-china-dietary-cadmium-exposure">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A third study found that eggs, powder or ground (all samples (EU Member State submissions)) had cadmium higher at 10.4 µg/kg, against 3.33 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (eggs, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe|20]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Cadmium dietary exposure in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.



<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for eggs

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/guo2024-duck-eggs-hg-mining-china|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guo Y, Li Y, Wang Q, Zhang H, Liu J, Feng X · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guo2024-duck-eggs-hg-mining-china">Heavy metal contamination in duck eggs near mercury mining areas in southwest China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/guo2024-duck-eggs-hg-mining-china">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

## Eggs FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-eggs" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-eggs" data-question="What heavy metals are found in eggs?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in eggs?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Zn, V, Se, As, B, Ba, F, Hg, I, Mg, Mo, S, Sr and Tl in eggs, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-eggs" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-eggs" data-question="How do heavy metals get into eggs?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into eggs?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, eggs from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than eggs from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wu et al. · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens">Ameliorative effects of selenized yeast on laying hen performance and heavy metal residues in eggs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Veterinary Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Eggs, as sold from basal diet + 5 mg Cd, 50 mg Pb, 3 mg Hg, 5 mg Cr per kg (HEM) (experiment) had lead higher at 1,000 µg/kg, against 920 µg/kg for hens fed corn-soybean meal basal diet (control, CON) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wu et al. · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens">Ameliorative effects of selenized yeast on laying hen performance and heavy metal residues in eggs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Veterinary Science</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wu2022-selenized-yeast-laying-hens">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-eggs" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-eggs" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in eggs?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in eggs?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, eggs, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (0.569 µg/kg) and the highest in SEARO (340 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (0.4 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (20.8 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-eggs" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-eggs" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in eggs?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in eggs?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same eggs.<sup class="cite">[[sources/wang2019-dietary-lead-guangzhou|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wang M, Liang B, Zhang W, Chen K, Zhang Y, Zhou H, Cheng Y, Liu H, Zhong X, Li Y, Liu Y · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wang2019-dietary-lead-guangzhou">Dietary Lead Exposure and Associated Health Risks in Guangzhou, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wang2019-dietary-lead-guangzhou">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Eggs, canned (all samples (Guangzhou, 2014-2017)) had lead lower at 4 µg/kg, against 6 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (eggs, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/wang2019-dietary-lead-guangzhou|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Wang M, Liang B, Zhang W, Chen K, Zhang Y, Zhou H, Cheng Y, Liu H, Zhong X, Li Y, Liu Y · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/wang2019-dietary-lead-guangzhou">Dietary Lead Exposure and Associated Health Risks in Guangzhou, China</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/wang2019-dietary-lead-guangzhou">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
